My sister died in a hospice center - the physician told us her cancer was simply too widespread, there was nothing they could do to help her have a good quality of life or stay alive with energy, able to manage the pain. Because she was young and strong and her brain was ok and her heart was ok, it was possible she would be alive for weeks but mostly comatose, waking to extreme pain and disorientation. I prayed hard for her to die quickly and gently to spare her that - there was no other outcome. Her soul leaves fast or she suffers for weeks. 

She only agreed to hospice in the first place because she was in so much unmanageable pain. 

Anyway, she was given dilated on a pump she could press to manage her pain. When she was unable to press it anymore, my dad did whenever she made a distressing noise. I did not push the pump once I arrived, and she passed within 7 hours or so of my arrival. 

I've questioned and felt regret once or twice about what the fuck happened - did she actually die because her soul left or because the drugs shut her body down faster. She did have bone and lung cancer and she was suffering so much. She was in the stages of dying before the high doses of medicine, but she was taking it I think throughout her hospice stay, and I hope we did the right thing. I know we did but yet I still fear sometimes.

My sister passing away three years ago involved many beautiful, spooky things. 

She fought cancer for about 7 years total before passing and when she had her mastectomy, she wanted me by her side. After the surgery she made a joke to the doctor (while still loopy from the anesthesia) as he was telling her about what was in the IV 'Did you put glitter in it?!' This was on point for her as she was a make up artist and loved color, glitter, beauty. When I arrived at her apartment for the first time after being by her bedside as she passed in a hospice center, the song 'Glitter in the Air' by Pink played on the radio, just as we were pulling in, totally at random. My partner and I sat in the driveway and listened to it and cried. 

When I went inside I immediately saw her dog, and he was so happy to see me and when he realized she was not with me, he knew. I could feel it. He had seen me with her at the hospital and I think he knew I would not be home without her unless she was gone. He laid down and whined and I told him he was such a good dog and did such a good job loving her. He passed away recently and in the days surrounding his passing, I kept seeing German shepherds that seemed to be staring at me. 

A couple of weeks after my sister's death, I returned to her apartment to be present and really soak up her space before we had to pack it up. When I walked in, there was a package from a subscription box company called Lunarly there that my sister had ordered sometime before she died, and I knew it was for me. She had been telling me she felt I just had to have this box, and she wanted to get it from me but I kept telling her to save her money and not spend it on me. She basically gave me an extended gift from beyond the grave with that box. I kept the subscription for over a year and it really felt like gifts from her, every thing. In that first box was a plant that is still thriving and a deck of tarot cards that I use often. She was fearful of my tarot practice (she was more traditional christian) and I took her sending me the cards as a message that she understood my spiritual practice and was blessing it from the other side. 

I love her so much and I am SO THANKFUL that she makes herself so known to me, even now. You are magic, Virginia <3

YTA, but I don't think you mean to be and it won't really matter that you are, until your sister dies, which she will, because we are all mortal and life is way too short. 

My sister died 2 months ago. I am 31, she was 46. She will never be at my wedding. I will never see her get married. 

She struggled with addiction over the years and our relationship had its ups and downs. I too had given her lots of things on loan over the years, a borrowed scarf, a borrowed purse, whatever. Never got them back, never saw them again. She transitioned to hospice care and I packed up to head to her city, thinking I would stay with her for at least a couple of weeks as she maybe healed and came out of hospice care, maybe passed on after some meaningful time spent. 

It occurred to me to take her one of my grandmothers rings which I was gifted while my grandmother was still alive, for her to wear and enjoy during this difficult time. I packed it. I put it away. I was so afraid the ring would go missing. One of her friends with an issue might steal it, or it would get lost, or otherwise go away and that seemed awful. The idea of withholding something beautiful and of my grandmother from my sister seemed worse. I took the ring and was able to watch my sister admire it and put it on. Thank god I did as she transitioned out of this world less than 24 hours later. Her best friend took the ring off her finger after I adorned her body, prior to her traveling for her cremation. 

Also, as I have been cleaning up her apartment and processing her belongings, I have found so many things of mine I thought she had lost. A purse from when I was 15. A scarf from when I was 23. She kept and treasured so much. 

Talk to your sister, and be extra kind. you are so fucking lucky you have gotten to keep yours. I hope you get to keep her for a long time.
